sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian verbs change according to the subject. Common first-person forms end in -ok/-ek/-ök, chosen the same way a plural or any other suffix is — by vowel harmony.

If Hungarian verbs feel like they’re shape-shifting on you, that’s fair — dolgozom and tanulok share almost nothing on the surface even though both simply mean ‘I [verb].’ Treat each new verb’s ‘I’ form as its own small vocabulary item at first; the patterns only start feeling predictable after you’ve collected a handful of examples.
